rule_semantics.run_length: sum over variable_runs entries of (at + element_length), plus the tail of the last entry for that slot
rule_semantics.at: constant filler bytes from the current cursor to the start of this element; the cursor starts at the beginning of the run and advances past each element
rule_semantics.tail: constant bytes from the end of this element to the end of the run; only the last entry for a slot carries a non-zero tail
rule_semantics.tail_by_version: an exact document version override for tail bytes when a variable run ends differently across file generations
rule_semantics.string: Native swccu.dll CString framing. A single MFC length prefix is u8 below 0xff, ff + u16 below 0xfffe, or ff ff ff + u32 otherwise; it is followed by that many ANSI bytes. Unicode strings start with ff fe ff, then carry a second length prefix and that many UTF-16LE code units.
rule_semantics.count: count_width bytes of count at the cursor, then stride bytes per element, so count_width + stride*count
rule_semantics.conditional: predicate_width bytes read at predicate_at relative to the cursor; the element is width bytes when the value is in values and 0 bytes otherwise; predicate_at bytes are part of at
rule_semantics.guard: predicate_width bytes read at predicate_at relative to the cursor; the run is refused unless the value is in values, then at plus tail bytes are consumed
rule_semantics.opaque: length is not computable from the bytes at hand; a segmenter must refuse rather than guess
rule_semantics.groups: an ordered chain of counted child groups for a class whose body is a sequence of loops rather than a fixed slot list; each group reads its count out of the stream at count.back bytes ahead of its first element as a count.width scalar, walks that many copies of element, and consumes trailer bytes after the last one
rule_semantics.repeat: a group whose element count is a constant rather than a stream field
rule_semantics.repeat_trailer: fixed bytes consumed once after the final element of a resolved repeated child sequence
rule_semantics.element_by_version: a group element whose runs differ per document version, keyed by the exact version the stream carries, falling through to element when the version is not named

After the six recovered child groups, a fully bounded sgSketch is followed by its parent's next token without consuming it. The directly traced values are null, class references 0x80bb and 0x8131 in the two older vendor parts, or a class definition marker. The guard accepts only those witnessed values. sgSketch.repeat_note: sgSketch does not have a fixed child arity and its children are not one repeated template either: the body is an ordered chain of counted loops, each with its own count read out of the stream just ahead of it, its own multi child element, and its own trailing filler. sgSketch::Serialize at 0x4c5d28c0 reads the counts itself and delegates the tagged reads: specialised to document version 18000 it holds 68 do/while loops and 41 scalar reads but only four tagged reads, and each loop is opened by a su_CArchive::AR_get_int or AR_get_ushort that also sizes the destination array immediately before the loop, exactly as at lines 630, 635 and 667 of the specialised body, while the loop body calls FUN_4c5d0b70, FUN_4c5cc540, FUN_4c5e1e30 and friends to do the ReadObject work. That is why the rsp column of the traces places every ReadObject one and two frames below sgSketch::Serialize and yet the counts are still in sgSketch::Serialize's own frame, and why the count of each group sits a fixed distance ahead of the group rather than at a fixed offset in the lead. FUN_4c5e1e30, the single dimension list callee, shows the same shape one level down: fourteen AR_get_ushort reads, each immediately driving a do/while whose body is one ReadObject. The six groups below reproduce the child offsets of all twenty traced sgSketch instances whose scopes are fully derivable, at document versions 14000 and 18000, with zero residual against the recorded scope_end. The four incompletely bounded instances now stop at the terminal tag guard instead of letting the last child absorb unknown sketch payload. The counts are shipped as u16 because that is the only width the point group admits at its offset; the relation, constraint and chain counts admit either two or four bytes there, since no traced instance carries a count above 4.

groups.name: entity
groups.note: the entity loop. Each element is four tagged reads: two null slots that carry an 8 byte and a 39 byte run, the entity handle, and the entity itself whose 87 byte run closes with the inline moLineViz_c record the 0x800 < version gate takes. The count is the u16 EntityCount at offset 0 of the 49 byte lead, which is 49 bytes ahead of the first element. Across the traced instances counts 1 and 4 are witnessed.

groups.name: point
groups.note: the sketch line loop. Each element is two tagged reads with ordinary scalar runs of 8 and 80 bytes. A concrete sgPointHandle consumes its own handle body; the first slot has a four-byte enclosing scalar record and the second has none. For null children, the first run is empty at sentinel 0xffff0000, is 17 bytes at variant 0x09000000, and is empty for the all-zero terminal record. The second run is 16 bytes at sentinel 0xffffffff, 10 bytes at variant 0xffff0002, and 26 bytes at sentinel 0xffff0000. Otherwise its discriminator at byte 16 selects three decompiled member variants: value 0x0100 occupies 100 bytes at document generation 14000 and 103 at 18000, paired value 0x03000300 occupies 89 bytes, and value 0x0600 occupies 79 bytes. The ordinary group closes with its 13 byte trailer; an all-zero final second record selects the serializer's terminal branch and has no trailer. When the preceding point's second contour handle is present, its ten-byte sgEntHandle body and the enclosing scalar record place the u16 count 12 bytes behind the first line child. When that handle is null, the count begins at the group cursor and the first line's ten-byte prefix places the child 12 bytes later. Both paths follow FUN_4c5d0b70 and sgSketch::Serialize at 0x4c5d28c0; the traced counts are 0, 1, 4 and 5.

groups.name: relation
groups.note: the first relation loop. Each element is four tagged reads: ordinarily a null slot with no run, a 16 byte handle record, a 17 byte record at document version 18000 and 16 bytes at 14000, and the relation handle followed by 4 bytes. The legacy 14000 serializer also selects a geometry-backed member branch: a leading u32 value 4 occupies 8 bytes in slots zero and two, discriminator 0x08000400 occupies 100 bytes in slot one, and discriminator 0x06000500 occupies 89 bytes in slot three and closes without the ordinary two-byte trailer. The count is the u16 6 bytes ahead of the loop, inside the run that closes the point group. Across the traced instances counts 1 and 4 are witnessed.

groups.name: constraint
groups.note: the second relation loop, read as nine tagged reads per element with the runs 0, 16, 17, 0, 4, 26, 0, 0 and 6. The count is the u16 6 bytes ahead of the loop. Only document version 18000 exercises this loop in the traces, so its element is not version gated; the 14000 parts all carry a count of zero here. Across the traced instances counts 0 and 1 are witnessed.

groups.name: lists
groups.note: the two suObList children the sketch always reads after the relation loops, with the 170 byte and 38 byte runs that separate them. groups.name: chain

moCompFeature_c.note: The only slot holds this class single child, a classref to moUnitComponent_c that the traces record as external#43 in eight parts and external#45 in vendor_cojinete. re/data/Layouts/ExternalClasses.json slot component measures that class at own_body_lengths [0] with one nested object reference of traced_span_lengths [2], so the whole child subtree is 4 bytes: 2 for the classref tag, 0 of own body and 2 for the object reference. The traced scope from the end of this class own tag is 93 bytes in the 18000-era authored parts and 89 bytes in the 13000/14000-era vendor parts, so run 0 is 93 - 4 = 89 at document version 18000 and 89 - 4 = 85 at 14000 and 13000. Consecutive instances are 119 bytes apart in the authored parts and 115 in the vendor parts, so the array length is 93 + 119*(n-1) or 89 + 115*(n-1) by generation. moCompFeature_c::Serialize itself contributes at most two i32 flags, both gated on moArchiveHelper_c::hasCondition bits set by the caller rather than by the stream, and then FUN_4bbb16e0, which for ver >= 0x4a5 reads only the i32 tree node id and a su_CTime, 8 bytes, matching the id at end-8 and the time_t at end-4. The length is gated on the document version rather than on a positional predicate because a predicate inside this run would have to be read at an offset that depends on the run length being computed.

moCompSketchEntHandle_c.note: Run 0 carries the same moCompFeature_c post-child body as moCompFeature_c and moCompRefPlane_c, and it inherits the same version gate for the same reason: slot 0 holds a moUnitComponent_c classref that ExternalClasses.json pins to a 4-byte subtree, so the bytes the tracer attributes to that child belong to this run. The generated table recorded run 0 as 0 because SolveRuns.py let the classref absorb them, which put the sgPointHandle in slot 1 exactly 89 bytes too early in the 18000-era circle trace and 85 too early in both 14000-era vendor traces. The three witnesses are CIRCLE_r10 at 18000, where the recorded gap from the end of the object reference at 6468 to the sgPointHandle classref at 6557 is 89 bytes, and vendor_cojinete and vendor_ring at 14000, where the same gap is 85. Those are the only three traced instances, and they agree with the 89/85 split moCompFeature_c already declares. The class stays partial because no traced instance carries a 13000-era witness, so a 13000 stream refuses this run with the version named rather than taking the 85 that moCompFeature_c records for that generation.
